title: Claims that Bix, Red Nichols and Berigan copied the Original Dixieland Jazz Band
summary: He says New Orleans players now imitate Bix, Nichols and Berigan, who in turn copied him, and that later men had records to work from.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: These people tell you it's a great big secret. It's nothing but march time, syncopated. White man's music and not colored. That's all it is. You take the tiger rank, we'll fit in that. You play. Hold that tiger. Hold that tiger. You can do anything you want with it. It's waking up different embellishments on a chord construction. That's all it is. Now these fellas in New Orleans, they play today. You know who they play? I'm going to let you know who they play. They're great. I was nobody. They play Big Spider-Back. They play Red Nichols. And they play Bonnie Berrigan. And if you don't believe what I tell you, they play the three of them together. And so all of them copied from Nick LaRock and admitted. In fact, I started Big Spider-Back on the horn. And you must study his records and listen to his endings. And he developed a style of music. That's from the ostrich walk. The same as Louis Armstrong's attack. And the same as the rest of them modern men who'd taken from the records, which they had something to work on. I didn't. All I had was ragtime music that was played by note to play with. And I had to make my own. And these fellas had something to work with. And it's an easy thing when you can lay out on record and play alongside of it. You can play a contra melody. You can play against it. And you can make up your own style when you have something already started for you.
